chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Ubayd ibn Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man marries off his grandson's daughter, it is valid upon his son (the father). He also said: And the son (the father) also has the right to marry her off. If her father desires a man and her grandfather desires a man, then the grandfather is more entitled to her marriage. And the young girl is not consulted in that matter if she is between her parents (i.e., under their guardianship). But if she is a divorcee or widow (thayyib), then she is more entitled to herself.

key_terms.بَيْنَ أَبَوَيْهَا: between her parents (under their joint guardianship)
key_terms.ثَيِّباً: a divorcee or widow (previously married woman)

ai.seo_question: Who has the primary right to arrange the marriage of a granddaughter: the father or the grandfather?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the hierarchy of marriage guardianship (*wilayah*), establishing the grandfather's precedence over the father when both are present, a key point in Shia jurisprudence regarding the *wali al-nikah*. It further distinguishes between the virgin girl (*bikr*), whose guardian may marry her off without explicit consent, and the previously married woman (*thayyib*), who retains the primary right to choose her spouse, reflecting the balance between paternal authority and female agency in marital contracts. This ruling underscores the practical application of consent in Shia fiqh, where the nature of the woman's marital status directly impacts the scope of the guardian's authority.
